chunks: Hariz from Ubayd ibn Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
When he extracts it from his wealth, so it gets wasted, and he had not specified it for anyone, so he is not accountable for it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zakat funds that are lost or wasted before reaching the recipient?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the transfer of risk (ghurm) in Zakat distribution; if the giver does not specify a recipient, the obligation is considered fulfilled upon dispatch, absolving the giver of liability for subsequent loss. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that Zakat is a debt on the giver's wealth that is discharged upon valid delivery, distinguishing it from general charity where retention of funds might imply continued responsibility.

en.hubeali:
Hareyz, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When he extracts it (Zakāt) from his wealth, so it gets wasted, and he had not specified it for anyone, so he is not accountable for it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Hariz has narrated from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one takes away Zakat from his assets but does not name the beneficiary and it is lost, he is free from his obligation.’”
